title: American runner wins L.A. Marathon by closest margin in history after sprint finish
content:
American runner Nathan Martin won the Los Angeles Marathon on Sunday by the closest margin in history after overtaking Kenya’s Michael Kimani Kamau by 0.01 seconds.

Martin, 36, finished in a time of 2 hours, 11 minutes, 17 seconds after a solo chase of the Kenyan race leader from over a mile and a half out. Kimani Kamau collapsed after being beaten at the line and was carried off on a stretcher by medical personnel.

Martin, who works as a high school track and cross-country coach, finished the 26.2 mile race only 32 seconds off his 2:10:45 marathon personal best, which he clocked in 2023 at the Grandma’s Marathon.

“I made an actual move five miles out … when I saw no one else was picking up the pace. I decided I needed to push,” Martin said, per the LA Times. “At a mile and a half to go, I could see the leader and with 800 meters to go, I was thinking, ‘I’m catching him.’”

The L.A. Marathon, while not an official major, is one of the largest marathons in the United States since its inception in 1986 and on Sunday 27,000 runners took to the streets. 45-year-old Olympian Priscah Cherono was the first to cross the line in the women’s category, beating her competition with a time of 2:25:19. The Kenyan was only two seconds off her personal best, set in December.

Cherono, on International Women’s Day, also won a $10,000 bonus for being the first runner, male or female, to cross the line with the women starting 15:45 before the men.
